text: Dara's flat is above the bakery on Quill Street and the door code changes every month.
The cat is called Biscuit and she is allergic to chicken-flavoured treats.
Passport renewal for the fictional Marrow Islands is due before the 14th of March.
Swims at the Harbourside pool on Tuesday and Thursday mornings around 7:15.
Prefers tea with oat milk and no sugar, never coffee after 3 PM.
The group project for HIST3050 is about medieval salt trade routes and is led by Wren.
Do not call the library at weekends, it is closed; check the online catalogue instead.
The Anvil Cafe is also called the forge by friends, on Copper Row near the tram stop.
Bike lock combination was changed to a four-digit date of the first moon landing.
Usually walks home along the canal on Fridays after the pottery class.
Wears size ten running shoes and likes the grey trail pair for wet days.
Brother Tobias visits on the second weekend of December and sleeps on the sofa bed.
The landlord, Mr Okonkwo-Reyes, wants rent paid by the 3rd via bank transfer.
When planning study blocks, never put them right after a late shift; leave a two hour gap.
The Hollow is the nickname for the basement study room in the Granary building.
Allergic to hazelnuts, carries the blue pen injector in the left jacket pocket.
Favourite album for focus work is a slow instrumental piano record by Imre Valk.
Sunday evenings are for meal prep: rice, roasted peppers and lentil soup for the week.
The cert exam for the cloud course is booked at the Lindgren test centre on the 22nd.
Grandmother Ilse's birthday is the 9th of May; she likes lilies, not roses.
Say times as 8:11 PM in the evening, never 24-hour format.
Gym is Fenwick Hall, the second floor weights room, locker number 41.
Laptop charger is the 96 watt one; the spare lives in the green drawer under the printer.
Reads a chapter of a novel before bed, currently a mystery set in a lighthouse.
Learning Portuguese with a ten minute lesson every day on the phone.
